item.title: Budget, personalisation shape Indian travellers' choices: Booking.com
item.description: A Booking.com report reveals that Indian travellers increasingly prioritise budgets, emotional preferences and unconventional experiences when planning holidays for 2027 ...
item.dc:creator: Hemlata Samant
item.content:encoded: Indian travellers are increasingly planning trips around emotional states, strict budget filters and unconventional experiences, with almost 89 per cent of them interested in choosing a holiday specifically to do something completely out of character, while 65 per cent are keen to surprise their friends and family with their choice of destination, according to a report by Booking.com. The report, titled “Expect the Unexpected”, included data from more than 28,000 travellers across 32 countries and territories, including 1,005 travellers from India, alongside employee insights on how people search. The study was conducted between July and August 2026. Budget considerations influenced family travel decisions. The data revealed that almost 75 per cent of Indian travellers reconsidered whom to invite on trips due to differences in spending habits, while around 74 per cent of Indian parents said they were interested in travelling without children so they could spend more on themselves. “Travel in 2027 is becoming deeply personal, with Indian travellers increasingly planning trips around their innermost passions. From stepping outside comfort zones to rethinking travel companions and picking destinations based on how they want to feel, travellers are actively challenging conventional ways of exploring the world,” said Santosh Kumar, regional manager, South Asia, at Booking.com. The report also highlighted that travel is increasingly being viewed as an opportunity to strengthen personal relationships. About 96 per cent of Indian travellers said at least one holiday activity had helped them have honest or difficult conversations, while 71 per cent said they would consider taking a trip to resolve conflicts or arguments. Walking or hiking together emerged as one of the most effective activities for facilitating such conversations. Health and lifestyle considerations influenced holiday planning as well. About 92 per cent of respondents said at least one health, body or lifestyle change had influenced their choice of destination or holiday activities in recent years. Further, 85 per cent said their dietary preferences would influence their choice of accommodation or destination. The report also revealed growing interest in activity-led travel. Around 90 per cent of Indian travellers who had travelled alone said participating in a shared physical activity or challenge had helped them form lasting connections or friendships. Further, 83 per cent expressed interest in joining communities of like-minded people while travelling. In addition, personalisation emerged as another factor, with 93 per cent of Indian travellers saying they would choose a holiday destination primarily based on how they want to feel rather than where they want to go.

item.title: Nvidia scandal: Jensen Huang signals willingness to return as CEO
item.description: Board creates national security panel; interim CEO Colette Kress keeps day-to-day oversight as committee meets at least quarterly ...
item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / Nvidia scandal: Jensen Huang signals willingness to return as CEO

Nvidia scandal: Jensen Huang signals willingness to return as CEO Board creates national security panel; interim CEO Colette Kress keeps day-to-day oversight as committee meets at least quarterly

Jensen Huang | Image: Bloomberg

Reuters 4 min read Last Updated : Nov 17 2026 | 9:58 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Nvidia's former CEO Jensen Huang, who resigned from the chipmaker last week under a cloud of scandal, said on Tuesday he "would be honored" to come back as CEO if the board decided his return would be in the best interest of shareholders and employees.   "Since my departure, I've seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA's employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO," Huang said in his first public statement since he resigned on November 12 over revelations of extramarital affairs that intensified scrutiny of the chip firm's China business.   "I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board's independent investigation," he said.

Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Huang's statement. Nvidia shares pared some declines and were last down 1%.   Earlier in the day Nvidia created a board-level committee to oversee national security and export controls, its first major governance move since Huang left. Also Read

When founders lose control: Tech leaders pushed out of their companies

US moves to restrict China's remote access to AI chips after Nvidia row

Nvidia board not considering Jensen Huang's return as CEO: Report

Company-sponsored visa movements to decline significantly, says IBM CEO premium

Jensen Huang to return as Nvidia CEO? Over 160,000 back his comeback

Huang's relationships, including one with a woman suspected of spying for China, have raised questions about whether Nvidia's oversight kept pace with its rapid growth and increasing importance to US national security. The crisis had erased more than $400 billion from the company's market value by Monday's close.   The National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee will be chaired by director Suzanne Nora Johnson, a former Goldman Sachs vice chair, Nvidia said. Directors Stephen Neal, former CEO of law firm Cooley, and John Dabiri, a Caltech professor, will also serve on the committee.

US President Donald Trump welcomed the move, calling the launch of a national security initiative a good idea.   TIGHTENING CHINA CHIP CURBS   The committee's creation comes a day after the Trump administration said it would further restrict China's access to advanced AI chips from companies including Nvidia, as Trump headed to China for talks with President Xi Jinping.   Washington has for years sought to curb Beijing's access to Nvidia's most advanced processors, putting the company's China business at the center of tensions over national security, trade and US technological leadership.   Chinese companies, however, have repeatedly found ways around the restrictions, while Huang had advocated allowing more chip exports to China.

US officials had raised concerns about Huang's relationship with Alice Huang, a former senior executive and controlling shareholder of Singapore-based cloud computing firm Megaspeed, whom US intelligence agencies suspect has links to Chinese intelligence.   Megaspeed has been under investigation over the possible diversion of restricted Nvidia chips to China and potential export-control violations. The company has denied wrongdoing.   Nvidia said the new committee will oversee its national security and global trade compliance programs and work with independent legal, national security and trade-compliance experts.   The company's National Security Team and Global Trade Compliance Team will report to the committee, while interim CEO Colette Kress will oversee day-to-day operations. The committee plans to meet at least quarterly, including with management and in executive sessions.

Nvidia did not have a chief compliance officer, according to its 2026 proxy statement.   It was not immediately clear whether the committee was created in response to the revelations about Huang's affairs.   Nvidia did not respond to a Reuters request for comment.   SECURITY, EXPORT CONTROLS UNDER BOARD WATCH   While major technology companies including Alphabet, Apple, Meta and Microsoft have board committees overseeing areas such as regulatory compliance, cybersecurity, privacy and strategy, Nvidia's new panel has a narrower mandate focused on national security and export controls, a structure more commonly associated with aerospace and defense companies.   "We are committed to working constructively with government and industry partners to help establish and advance a robust framework that uses every tool at our disposal to safeguard national security while supporting continued technological innovation," Nvidia board chairman Harvey Jones said.

Nvidia has also warned chip buyers in recent months that the proposed US Remote Access Security Act could expose the company and its customers to legal risks by expanding Washington's oversight of Chinese companies' access to AI chips through cloud services, CNBC reported on Tuesday.   Huang's daughter Madison Huang, who is a senior director of product marketing at Nvidia, was closely involved in shaping the public defence of the company's ties to Megaspeed, the Financial Times reported on Tuesday. She did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.   The company is due to report third-quarter earnings after the market closes on Tuesday.

item.title: Global stocks fall as Nvidia earnings, Anthropic debut put AI rally to test
item.description: Semiconductor shares led losses across major markets, with US chipmakers falling 5.3 per cent and stocks in South Korea and Taiwan declining 3.6 per cent and 6 per cent, respectively ...
item.content:encoded:
Home / Markets / News / Global stocks fall as Nvidia earnings, Anthropic debut put AI rally to test

Global stocks fall as Nvidia earnings, Anthropic debut put AI rally to test Semiconductor shares led losses across major markets, with US chipmakers falling 5.3 per cent and stocks in South Korea and Taiwan declining 3.6 per cent and 6 per cent, respectively

Analysts expect earnings growth of 90 per cent on revenue of $109 billion in Nvidia's fiscal third quarter, and investors are watching whether the new management will stick to the chipmaker's bullish outlook | Image: Bloomberg

Reuters NEW YORK/LONDON 4 min read Last Updated : Nov 17 2026 | 7:58 AM IST

Listen to This Article

Stock indexes fell across major global markets on Monday, weighed down by semiconductor shares, with Nvidia earnings and Anthropic's market debut this week set to test whether the AI-fuelled bull market has further to run. US chipmakers dropped 5.3 per cent, while overnight in Korea and Taiwan stocks fell 3.6 per cent and 6 per cent respectively. MSCI's broadest index ended down 1.8 per cent while earlier, stocks in Europe ended down less than 0.3 per cent after rising 2.5 per cent to record highs last week. The dollar index touched its highest level since April 2025, as comments from Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh did not dent expectations for a rate hike next month.

Nvidia , which reports earnings after the bell on Tuesday, fell 4.1 per cent on Monday and is down nearly 24 per cent this month weighed down in part by the departure of its CEO, Jensen Huang, last week. Also Read

Stock Market LIVE: GIFT Nifty signals muted open; Asian markets decline on tech selloff

Stock Market Close: Sensex ends 512 pts higher, Nifty at 25,291; FMGC, bank shares outshine

Analysts expect earnings growth of 90 per cent on revenue of $109 billion in Nvidia's fiscal third quarter, and investors are watching whether the new management will stick to the chipmaker's bullish outlook for next year. "Nvidia may well deliver another exceptional beat and raise at tomorrow's earnings, but investors are increasingly trying to value a business in FY2028 and FY2029 potentially without the individual who architected its competitive advantage," said Chris Weston, head of research at foreign exchange brokerage Pepperstone.

AI behemoth Anthropic is expected to raise up to $80 billion when it prices its IPO on Wednesday on a near $1.5 trillion valuation, and begins trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday under the ANT.O ticker. "The success of the IPO, along with Nvidia's earnings, will definitely be the barometer for whether the (stock market) correction will continue or not," said Nadia El Bilassy, senior market analyst at Equiti Group. At the close of trading in New York, the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 739.38 points, or 1.41 per cent, to 51,608.17, the S&P 500 fell 145.08 points, or 1.92 per cent, to 7,416.59 and the Nasdaq Composite fell 626.51 points, or 2.49 per cent, to 24,509.76.

Oil slips, greenback weighs The minutes of the US Federal Reserve's October policy meeting are due on Wednesday, while a parade of Fed officials will be speaking this week. Traders continue to price in a rate increase from the Fed at its December meeting, following a series of data that indicate inflation pressure is broadening. Fed funds futures imply a quarter-point rate hike next month, and markets are pricing in at least three rate hikes between now and the end of 2027. The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies, rose 0.19 per cent to 103.60, with the euro down 0.24 per cent at $1.0995.

Jefferies strategist Mohit Kumar does not see the case for a string of rate hikes, but said that "hawkish comments from Fed, ECB and BoE speakers have brought the prospect of aggressive hikes back on the table." He said the path beyond December would depend on the US war with Iran. "If we get any version of ceasefire in the Middle East and oil comes below $80, we do not see a case for further hikes in 2027," he said. Oil prices fell on signs of recovering oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz, though fresh tanker incidents underscored the potential for more volatility.

"While the elevated geopolitical tensions seem to have become the new norm, global oil supplies appear to be remaining relatively stable and the US is also running at near-record production," said Dennis Kissler at US financial services firm BOK Financial. US crude fell 3.59 per cent to $85.38 a barrel and Brent fell to $92.20 per barrel, down 3.8 per cent on the day. In government debt, the yield on benchmark US 10-year notes fell 2.39 basis points to 5.129 per cent, from 5.153 per cent late on Friday. The 30-year bond yield fell 0.69 basis points to 5.4741 per cent from 5.481 per cent.

In commodities, spot silver fell 3.68 per cent to $46.93 an ounce and US silver futures fell 4.38 per cent to $46.89 an ounce. Copper declined 1.43 per cent to $13,207.50 a ton. Spot gold fell 0.74 per cent to $3,851.44 an ounce, after touching its lowest level since October 2025 at $3,830.74 earlier in the session.

(Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

item.title: RBI reiterates listing mandate for Tata Sons, seeks compliance with norms
item.description: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has reiterated that Tata Sons must comply with all regulatory requirements applicable to upper-layer non-banking financial companies (NBFCs), including the mandatory ...
item.dc:creator: Subrata Panda
item.content:encoded: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has reiterated that Tata Sons must comply with all regulatory requirements applicable to upper-layer non-banking financial companies (NBFCs), including the mandatory stock market listing, in a communication to the Tata group holding company dated November 16. In a letter addressed to Tata Sons’ chief financial officer, the central bank referred to the company’s October 6 communication seeking regulatory guidance to ensure compliance with applicable regulations. The RBI said while Tata Sons had not sought clarification on any specific regulation or guideline, its request appeared to relate to the discussions at the company’s board regarding listing. “In this connection, you are advised to comply with all applicable regulations/ guidelines/ directions, issued by the RBI in respect of NBFCs in the Upper Layer (NBFC-UL), as stipulated in extant regulations/ guidelines/ directions hosted on the RBI’s website, including the requirement of listing by your company,” the letter said. The latest communication reinforces the regulator’s position on the listing of Tata Sons, which has remained unlisted despite the September 30, 2025, deadline prescribed for upper-layer NBFCs. The development assumes significance, coming ahead of Tata Sons board meeting on November 26. The November 16 letter follows the RBI’s September 11 decision to reject Tata Sons’ application seeking voluntary surrender of its registration as a core investment company (CIC). The rejection effectively closed the company’s principal regulatory route to exit the NBFC framework and avoid the listing requirement. Tata Sons had approached the RBI in March 2024 seeking deregistration after repaying all its debt. The company had sought to move out of the regulatory framework applicable to upper-layer NBFCs, which would have allowed it to remain privately held. However, the RBI rejected the application after examining the various aspects of the request and subsequently directed the company to comply with the regulations applicable to upper-layer NBFCs. Tata Sons was first classified as an upper-layer NBFC in September 2022 under the RBI’s scale-based regulatory framework. Entities classified in this category are subject to enhanced regulatory requirements, including mandatory listing within three years of their classification. Under the revised framework, NBFCs with assets of ₹1 trillion or more qualify for upper-layer classification. Tata Sons reported total assets of around ₹2.01 trillion as of March 31, 2026, placing it well above the prescribed threshold. The RBI had also retained Tata Sons in its list of upper-layer NBFCs for 2026-27, published this August, clarifying that its inclusion was without prejudice to the outcome of the company’s deregistration application, which was under examination at that time. Tata Trusts, which collectively control around 66 per cent of Tata Sons, have favoured retaining the holding company as a privately held entity. On the other hand, the Shapoorji Pallonji group, which holds around 18.37 per cent, has favoured a listing as a potential route to unlock value from its investment and facilitate fundraising against its stake.
